import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import os

# Suppress warnings
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Create submission directory
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
print("Loading data...")
train = pd.read_csv("./input/en_train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/en_test_2.csv")

print(f"Train shape: {train.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test.shape}")

# Split training data - hold out 10% for validation
np.random.seed(42)
indices = np.random.permutation(len(train))
val_size = int(0.1 * len(train))
val_indices = indices[:val_size]
train_fold_indices = indices[val_size:]

val_fold = train.iloc[val_indices].reset_index(drop=True)
train_fold = train.iloc[train_fold_indices].reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"Validation fold shape: {val_fold.shape}")
print(f"Training fold shape: {train_fold.shape}")

# Build compound model ONLY from training fold (not validation fold)
print("Building compound mode model on training fold only...")
final_compound_model = (
    train_fold.groupby(["before", "class"])["after"]
    .agg(lambda x: x.value_counts().index[0] if len(x) > 0 else np.nan)
    .to_dict()
)

# Build class inference lookup from training fold only
print("Building class inference lookup from training fold only...")
final_class_lookup = (
    train_fold.groupby("before")["class"]
    .agg(lambda x: x.value_counts().index[0])
    .to_dict()
)

# Global fallback for unknown combinations from training fold
global_mode = train_fold["after"].value_counts().index[0]
print(f"Global mode fallback: {global_mode}")

# CRITICAL FIX: Validate on hold-out set using inferred class (not ground truth)
# This matches the test inference logic
print("Validating on hold-out set with INFERRED class (matching test logic)...")
val_predictions = []
val_errors = []
for idx in range(len(val_fold)):
    before = val_fold.iloc[idx]["before"]
    true_class = val_fold.iloc[idx]["class"]

    # INFER class from before (same as test inference) - this is the fix!
    inferred_class = final_class_lookup.get(before, "PLAIN")

    # Use inferred_class for compound model lookup (NOT true_class)
    if (before, inferred_class) in final_compound_model:
        pred = final_compound_model[(before, inferred_class)]
    else:
        pred = global_mode

    val_predictions.append(pred)
    if pred != val_fold.iloc[idx]["after"]:
        val_errors.append(1)

val_accuracy = np.mean(val_errors)
print(
    f"Contamination-free Validation Accuracy (with inferred class): {val_accuracy:.6f}"
)

# Now build final model on ALL training data for test submission
print("Building final model on ALL training data for test submission...")
full_compound_model = (
    train.groupby(["before", "class"])["after"]
    .agg(lambda x: x.value_counts().index[0] if len(x) > 0 else np.nan)
    .to_dict()
)

full_class_lookup = (
    train.groupby("before")["class"].agg(lambda x: x.value_counts().index[0]).to_dict()
)

full_global_mode = train["after"].value_counts().index[0]

# Prepare test data
print("Preparing test submission...")
test["id"] = test["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + test["token_id"].astype(str)

# Predict on test set (same logic as validation now)
print("Making predictions on test set...")
final_test_preds = []
for idx in range(len(test)):
    before = test.iloc[idx]["before"]
    # Infer class from before (same as validation now)
    inferred_class = full_class_lookup.get(before, "PLAIN")

    if (before, inferred_class) in full_compound_model:
        pred = full_compound_model[(before, inferred_class)]
    else:
        pred = full_global_mode

    final_test_preds.append(pred)

# Save submission
print("Saving submission...")
output = pd.DataFrame({"id": test["id"], "after": final_test_preds})

# Verify format
print(f"Submission shape: {output.shape}")
print(f"Columns: {list(output.columns)}")
print(f"Sample predictions: {output['after'].head(10).tolist()}")
print(f"Sample IDs: {output['id'].head(10).tolist()}")

output.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")

# Verify file exists
if os.path.exists("./submission/submission.csv"):
    submission_check = pd.read_csv("./submission/submission.csv")
    print(f"Submission file loaded successfully: {submission_check.shape}")
    print(f"Submission header: {submission_check.columns.tolist()}")
else:
    print("ERROR: Submission file not created!")

print(f"\n=== Final Results ===")
print(f"Validation Accuracy (inferred class matching test logic): {val_accuracy:.6f}")
print(f"Test submission saved: ./submission/submission.csv")
plan: The previous solution has a critical validation mismatch where it uses ground-truth class labels from `val_fold["class"]` for model lookups, but test inference must infer class from "before" text alone using the class lookup. This means validation has privileged information, inflating accuracy by ~0.2-0.4%. I will fix this by computing the inferred class for each validation sample using the same class inference logic as test, then using this inferred class (not ground truth) for all model lookups during validation. This ensures validation and test use identical prediction paths and feature spaces, giving a realistic test-time performance estimate while the final model remains unchanged.
